package_info.package_manager: N/A (custom Linux malware, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: The malware systematically exploits up to 30 documented vulnerabilities in outdated WordPress plugins and themes on Linux servers. It injects malicious JavaScript into website files, enabling persistent client-side compromise, remote command execution, and further malware delivery, resulting in mass compromise of WordPress-based sites.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (post-exploitation on compromised Linux host, after initial access)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into WordPress PHP files (e.g., wp-content/themes/[theme]/functions.php) or deployed as a malicious binary on the server
required_permissions: filesystem (write access to WordPress files and directories)

malicious_snippets.code_language: python (pseudocode, actual malware likely C/C++ or shell)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the Linux host is compromised, the malware scans for outdated WordPress plugins and themes, exploits known vulnerabilities to gain write access, and injects a malicious JavaScript payload into website files, resulting in persistent client-side compromise and enabling remote command execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs automated scanning for vulnerable WordPress components and injects remote JavaScript into site files, a hallmark of mass web compromise campaigns.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate WordPress operation does not involve arbitrary scanning for vulnerabilities or unauthorized modification of plugin/theme files to inject external scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated patch management tools may scan for outdated plugins, but they do not inject or modify code within site files.
key_indicators: Automated exploitation of multiple CVEs in WordPress plugins/themes
Unauthorized modification of WordPress PHP files
Injection of external JavaScript references into site code
Network activity to attacker-controlled domains for payload delivery

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits an infected WordPress page)
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within WordPress site pages (e.g., in HTML output or theme/plugin files)
required_permissions: network (browser fetches remote script from attacker domain)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At page load, when a visitor accesses a compromised WordPress page, the injected JavaScript is fetched from a remote attacker-controlled domain and executed in the user's browser, enabling credential theft, drive-by downloads, or further exploitation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code loads and executes JavaScript from an untrusted, attacker-controlled domain, which is a classic indicator of a compromised website and enables client-side attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate WordPress sites should only load scripts from trusted sources or CDNs, not from unknown or suspicious external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Loading scripts from reputable CDNs (e.g., Google, Cloudflare) is common, but not from domains controlled by attackers.
key_indicators: Presence of <script src> tags referencing non-standard, suspicious domains
Execution of remote JavaScript in the context of site visitors
Potential for client-side data theft or malware delivery

attack_chain.action: Malware scans the Linux host for outdated WordPress plugins and themes by enumerating installed components and comparing versions against a list of known vulnerable releases.
attack_chain.leads_to: Identification of vulnerable plugins/themes for exploitation

attack_chain.action: Exploits up to 30 known vulnerabilities in detected outdated plugins/themes to gain unauthorized write access to WordPress files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify WordPress site files

attack_chain.action: Injects malicious JavaScript references into WordPress PHP or HTML files, modifying site output to include attacker-controlled scripts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is served to site visitors

attack_chain.action: Injected JavaScript loads additional payloads from attacker-controlled domains when users visit the compromised site, executing code in the browser context.
attack_chain.leads_to: Client-side compromise, credential theft, or further malware delivery

behavioral_signatures: Automated scanning of WordPress installation directories for plugin/theme versions
Mass modification of WordPress PHP or HTML files to inject external JavaScript references
Outbound network connections from the web server to attacker-controlled domains for script retrieval
file_indicators: Unexpected <script src> tags referencing non-standard domains in WordPress theme or plugin files (e.g., functions.php, header.php)
Modified timestamps or unauthorized changes in WordPress PHP files within wp-content/themes/ or wp-content/plugins/
Presence of unfamiliar JavaScript files in the webroot or within plugin/theme directories
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from the web server to domains such as 'malicious-domain.com' or other attacker infrastructure
Unusual traffic patterns from the web server to external IPs not associated with legitimate CDNs or plugin/theme update servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement file integrity monitoring on WordPress site files to detect unauthorized modifications, especially new or altered <script> tags referencing external domains. Regularly audit plugin and theme versions against known vulnerability databases. Analyze web server logs for outbound requests to suspicious or unrecognized domains. Use network monitoring to flag connections to attacker infrastructure. Employ automated tools to scan for the presence of injected JavaScript in site output and plugin/theme files.
